hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي لُبَابةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَهَى عَنْ قَتْلِ الْحَيَّاتِ الَّتِي فِي الْبُيُوتِ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Lubabah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of snakes that are in the houses.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ سَائِبَةَ مَوْلَاةٍ لِعَائِشَةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَهَى عَنْ قَتْلِ الْجِنَّانِ الَّتِي فِي الْبُيُوتِ ، إِلَّا ذَا الطُّفْيَتَيْنِ وَالْأَبْتَرَ ، فَإِنَّهُمَا يَخْطِفَانِ الْبَصَرَ وَيَطْرَحَانِ مَا فِي بُطُونِ النِّسَاءِ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sa'ibah, the freed slave of Aisha: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of the jinnan (house snakes) that are in the houses, except the one with two stripes and the short-tailed one, for indeed they both snatch away the eyesight and cause miscarriages in women.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ صَيْفِيٍّ مَوْلَى ابْنِ أَفْلَحَ ، عَنْ أَبِي السَّائِبِ مَوْلَى هِشَامِ بْنِ زُهْرَةَ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ فَوَجَدْتُهُ يُصَلِّي فَجَلَسْتُ أَنْتَظِرُهُ حَتَّى قَضَى صَلَاتَهُ ، فَسَمِعْتُ تَحْرِيكًا تَحْتَ سَرِيرٍ فِي بَيْتِهِ فَإِذَا حَيَّةٌ فَقُمْتُ لِأَقْتُلَهَا ، فَأَشَارَ أَبُو سَعِيدٍ أَنِ اجْلِسْ فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ أَشَارَ إِلَى بَيْتٍ فِي الدَّارِ ، فَقَالَ : أَتَرَى هَذَا الْبَيْتَ ؟ فَقُلْتُ : نَعَمْ ، قَالَ : إِنَّهُ قَدْ كَانَ فِيهِ فَتًى حَدِيثُ عَهْدٍ بِعُرْسٍ ، فَخَرَجَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلَى الْخَنْدَقِ ، فَبَيْنَا هُوَ بِهِ إِذْ أَتَاهُ الْفَتَى يَسْتَأْذِنُهُ ، فَقَالَ : يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، ائْذَنْ لِي أُحْدِثُ بِأَهْلِي عَهْدًا ، فَأَذِنَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، وَقَالَ : خُذْ عَلَيْكَ سِلَاحَكَ فَإِنِّي أَخْشَى عَلَيْكَ بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ ، فَانْطَلَقَ الْفَتَى إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فَوَجَدَ امْرَأَتَهُ قَائِمَةً بَيْنَ الْبَابيْنِ فَأَهْوَى إِلَيْهَا بِالرُّمْحِ لِيَطْعُنَهَا وَأَدْرَكَتْهُ غَيْرَةٌ ، فَقَالَتْ : لَا تَعْجَلْ حَتَّى تَدْخُلَ وَتَنْظُرَ مَا فِي بَيْتِكَ ؟ فَدَخَلَ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِحَيَّةٍ مُنْطَوِيَةٍ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ ، فَرَكَزَ فِيهَا رُمْحَهُ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ بِهَا فَنَصَبَهُ فِي الدَّارِ ، فَاضْطَرَبَتِ الْحَيَّةُ فِي رَأْسِ الرُّمْحِ ، وَخَرَّ الْفَتَى مَيِّتًا فَمَا يُدْرَى أَيُّهُمَا كَانَ أَسْرَعَ مَوْتًا الْفَتَى أَمْ الْحَيَّةُ ؟ فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ : إِنَّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ جِنًّا قَدْ أَسْلَمُوا ، فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ شَيْئًا فَآذِنُوهُ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ ، فَإِنْ بَدَا لَكُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَاقْتُلُوهُ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْطَانٌ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu al-Sa'ib, the freed slave of Hisham ibn Zuhrah, that he said: I entered upon Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and found him praying, so I sat waiting for him until he finished his prayer. Then I heard a movement under a bed in his house, and behold it was a snake, so I stood up to kill it. Abu Sa'id gestured to me to sit down. When he finished, he pointed to a house in the courtyard and said: Do you see this house? I said: Yes. He said: Indeed there was in it a young man recently married, and he went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the Trench (Battle of the Trench). While he was there, the young man came to him seeking permission, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, give me permission to visit my family. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him permission and said: Take your weapon with you, for I fear for you from Banu Qurayzah. So the young man went to his family and found his wife standing between the two doors. He aimed at her with the spear to stab her, as jealousy overcame him. She said: Do not be hasty until you enter and see what is in your house. So he entered and behold there was a snake coiled on his bed. He thrust his spear into it, then went out with it and set it up in the courtyard. The snake writhed at the top of the spear, and the young man fell down dead. It is not known which of them died first, the young man or the snake. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: Indeed in Madinah there are jinn who have accepted Islam, so when you see anything of them, give them warning for three days, and if they appear to you after that, then kill them, for they are only devils.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، كَانَ إِذَا وَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ فِي الْغَرْزِ وَهُوَ يُرِيدُ السَّفَرَ ، يَقُولُ : بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ ، اللَّهُمَّ ازْوِ لَنَا الْأَرْضَ وَهَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا السَّفَرَ ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ ، وَمِنْ كَآبَةِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ ، وَمِنْ سُوءِ الْمَنْظَرِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ
hadiths.english_translation: It reached Malik that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he placed his foot in the stirrup intending to travel: In the name of Allah. O Allah, You are the Companion in the journey and the Guardian of the family. O Allah, fold up for us the earth and make the journey easy for us. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of the journey, from gloomy return, and from evil appearance in wealth and family.

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Khawlah bint Hakim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Whoever stops at a stopping place and says: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created, nothing will harm him until he departs from that place.

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by the grandfather of Amr ibn Shu'ayb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The single rider is a devil, and the two riders are two devils, and the three are a riding party.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ : لَا يَحِلُّ لِامْرَأَةٍ تُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ، تُسَافِرُ مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ ، إِلَّا مَعَ ذِي مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهَا
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel the distance of a day and a night, except with a mahram (male guardian) from her family.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدٍ مَوْلَى سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ ، يَرْفَعُهُ : إِنّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ ، وَيَرْضَى بِهِ وَيُعِينُ عَلَيْهِ مَا لَا يُعِينُ عَلَى الْعُنْفِ ، فَإِذَا رَكِبْتُمْ هَذِهِ الدَّوَابَّ الْعُجْمَ ، فَأَنْزِلُوهَا مَنَازِلَهَا ، فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْأَرْضُ جَدْبَةً فَانْجُوا عَلَيْهَا بِنِقْيِهَا ، وَعَلَيْكُمْ بِسَيْرِ اللَّيْلِ ، فَإِنَّ الْأَرْضَ تُطْوَى بِاللَّيْلِ مَا لَا تُطْوَى بِالنَّهَارِ ، وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالتَّعْرِيسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ ، فَإِنَّهَا طُرُقُ الدَّوَابِّ وَمَأْوَى الْحَيَّاتِ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Khalid ibn Ma'dan, raising it to the Prophet ﷺ: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Gentle and loves gentleness, and He is pleased with it and assists with it in a way He does not assist with harshness. So when you ride these mute animals, give them their rest stops. If the land is barren, then hasten through it with their remaining strength. And upon you is night travel, for the earth is folded at night in a way it is not folded during the day. And beware of resting on the road, for it is the path of animals and the abode of snakes.

reliabilityIssues: Mursal - Khalid ibn Ma'dan is from the Tabi'in and the chain to the Prophet ﷺ is not mentioned

chainIssues: The expression 'يَرْفَعُهُ' (yarfa'uhu - he raises it) indicates that Khalid ibn Ma'dan is attributing this to the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning his source, making this mursal

plainChains: Malik ibn Anas -> Abu Ubayd -> Khalid ibn Ma'dan -> [disconnected] -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: The term 'يَرْفَعُهُ' (yarfa'uhu) indicates a mursal narration where Khalid ibn Ma'dan (a Tabi'i) is raising the hadith to the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning the intermediary
potential_issues.impact: This is a significant weakness as the missing link(s) between Khalid ibn Ma'dan and the Prophet ﷺ cannot be verified. This creates a clear disconnection in the chain

potential_issues.issue: Khalid ibn Ma'dan is from the Tabi'in generation and did not meet the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: Confirms the mursal nature of this narration

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'عَنْ' in the earlier part of the chain
potential_issues.impact: Minor concern given the reliability of those narrators

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ سُمَيٍّ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ : السَّفَرُ قِطْعَةٌ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ يَمْنَعُ أَحَدَكُمْ نَوْمَهُ وَطَعَامَهُ وَشَرَابَهُ ، فَإِذَا قَضَى أَحَدُكُمْ نَهْمَتَهُ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ فَلْيُعَجِّلْ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Travel is a piece of torment; it prevents one of you from his sleep, his food, and his drink. So when one of you fulfills his purpose from his journey, let him hasten back to his family.
